Its only gate logs are /home/ITER/mcintos/.local/share/imas-codex/gate-logs/held-names-refine-pass/green-1318561.log (checked 151 names, 38 accepted, 10 sourceless; EXIT=0) and red-1318562.log (FAIL accepted: graph 38, evidence 39; EXIT=1), and the red arm is the gate's own injected control rather than a failing test, so the added-failure set is empty.

assertion_analysis.failure_condition: The assertion expected_accepted compared against the graph's own resolve_all lineage walk fails whenever the evidence records a row as accepted on both axes that the live graph does not hold at the resolved identity. The recorded red arm reinstated exactly that condition with --inject-accepted 1 and the gate printed FAIL accepted: graph 38, evidence 39 and EXIT=1.

The live-identity assertion fires when the graph's deepest accepted responsibility set differs from the artefact's live_id, for instance after a rename moves a successor; it fails independently of the artefact because the walk is recomputed from the graph, though it reproduces any error in the rule itself.

The docs-score assertion reddens when a recorded docs score disagrees with s.reviewer_score_docs by more than 1e-6; it is skipped when either side is null, and a read-only probe of all 8 null rows found the graph also holds no docs score at their live identities, so the skip hides nothing in this artefact.

The sourceless assertion fails whenever the repository's own count_live_names_without_source differs from the artefact's recorded value — an independent source on both sides, so a drifted graph or an edited count reddens it; no negative control exercises it.

The spend assertion fails only when the artefact records a total above the ceiling it also records; it cannot fail on a true ledger spend above 20 recorded as below it, since both sides come from the same document. This assertion does not name an independent source.

The figure refuses (SystemExit) when the outcome split it recomputes from the rows sums to a different count than the by-hold-kind table records, so a hand-edited JSON reddens the regeneration rather than drawing a wrong bar.

findings.text: The gate file is outside the node's four declared write paths — docs/evidence/fragments/sn-definitions-by-construction/held-names-refine-pass.json, .html and .py plus docs/figures/sn-held-names-refine-pass — so the landed diff carries a fifth path the fence did not grant; the coordinator must widen the declared paths to the fragment directory or the gate must move.

The open-holds table is closed with parts.append("

") instead of "", so the delivered held-names-refine-pass.html:22 ends that table with an orphan closing paragraph and the table element is left unclosed in a committed artefact.

The by-hold-kind header row declares four cells (<th>Hold kind</th><th>Names</th><th>Accepted</th><th>Spend (USD)</th>) while each row emits five (<td> for the per-name rate at :588), so the delivered table's last column — the per-name USD rate the figure draws beside it — carries no header.

total_spend is summed over spend_by_name, which credits one LLMCost row to every id in standard_name_ids, so the per-kind spend column sums to 15.348296 while the headline total reads 11.564196 — 3.7841 USD (33%) more than the total stated beside the ceiling, and neither the HTML nor the JSON says the column is a non-partition of shared rename cost.

The spend assertion compares two fields of the artefact it just read (doc["spend"]["total_usd"] > doc["spend"]["ceiling_usd"]), so a total recorded below the ledger's true spend passes, and no negative control exercises this branch — the recorded red arm only injects into the accepted count.

LINEAGE, SUCCESSORS, pick_live and resolve_all are verbatim copies of held-names-refine-pass.py:180-244, and no test asserts the copies agree, so the docstring's claim that the gate re-reads 'by the report's own lineage rule' is a claim about two independent texts rather than about one shared owner.

The gate result is recorded under a gate: key with the command only described, and the manifest carries no tests: line, so promotion cannot rebuild its gate receipt from the record and must fall back to the commit message.
